renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_class_heatmap
  title: Drug class by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is the number of hits of one drug class in one sample, with the tool reporting the class most often and the number of distinct genes it covers as row annotations. It answers which resistance classes each sample carries.
    How to read: a dark row is a class found in most samples and a dark column a sample with a broad resistance profile. The side strips tell you whether a class rests on one tool and on how many genes.
    Note: tool vocabularies are folded onto one leading class per row, so very similar classes can still appear on separate rows.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: drug_class
    row_annotation_cols:
    - top_tool
    - n_genes_band

- component: table
  title: Drug class counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a drug class with its hit count per sample, its leading tool and the number of genes it covers. It answers the exact counts behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort by a sample column to see its main classes.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_heatmap
  title: Resistance gene by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is the number of hits of one resistance gene in one sample, with the gene's most frequent drug class as a row annotation. It answers which genes each sample carries and which are shared.
    How to read: a dark row is a gene found across samples and a dark column a sample with many resistance genes. Samples that cluster together share a resistance profile, which can point to a common source.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: gene_symbol
    row_annotation_cols:
    - drug_class_primary

- component: table
  title: Gene counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a resistance gene with its hit count per sample and its drug class. It answers the exact counts behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort by a sample column to see its main genes.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_dot_plot
  title: Gene support per sample
  description: |-
    Each dot is a resistance gene in a sample: its size is the share of screening tools that called the gene and its colour is the mean identity of the hits. It answers how well supported each detection is.
    How to read: large, strongly coloured dots are genes called by many tools at high identity and are the most trustworthy. Small dots are called by one tool only and are worth confirming with another screen or the original reads.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: gene_symbol
    mean_expression: mean_identity
    frac_expressing: tool_frac

- component: card
  title: Tools agreeing on a gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of screening tools that report a gene in a sample, and the histogram shows how many genes get one, two or more tools. It answers how much the tools agree.
    How to read: a pile at one tool means most calls rest on a single screen. A large share at several tools means a consistent resistome. The number of tools depends on how many the pipeline ran.
  column: n_tools
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its median and maximum

- component: card
  title: Identity of supported genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the mean percent identity of the hits for each gene in each sample, and the box shows the spread. It answers how close the detected genes are to known references.
    How to read: values near 100 percent are confident matches. A tail of low identities holds divergent homologues to check.
    Note: tools define identity at the nucleotide or amino acid level, so values are not strictly comparable across tools.
  column: mean_identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Gene support table
  description: |-
    Each row is a resistance gene in a sample with its hit count, the number of tools that agree and the mean identity and coverage. It answers the exact support behind each dot.
    How to read: sort by the number of tools to see the best supported genes first.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_island_track
  title: Resistance genes along contigs
  description: |-
    Each arrow is one resistance gene hit placed on its contig, pointing in the direction of the gene and coloured by the screening tool that reported it. It answers whether resistance genes sit together on the same contig.
    How to read: several arrows head to tail on one contig suggest a resistance island or a mobile cassette, which an aggregate over drug classes cannot show. Arrows of different colours on the same locus are the same gene found by several tools, so agreement between tools raises confidence in the call.
    Note: hAMRonization does not harmonise gene names or drug classes across tools, so one gene can appear under different symbols.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: gene_arrow_track
  roles:
    contig: contig
    feature_id: gene_symbol
    start: start
    end: stop
    strand: strand
    class: tool
    label: gene_symbol

- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_hierarchy
  title: Tool, drug class and gene hierarchy
  description: |-
    Each arc is a group of hits: the inner ring is the screening tool, the middle ring the drug class it reports and the outer ring the gene, sized by the number of hits and coloured by tool. It answers which tool contributes which part of the resistome.
    How to read: a wide arc in one tool and nothing in the others means that tool alone detects the class. Drug class names differ between tools, so the same class can appear as separate arcs under different tools; compare within a tool. Click an arc to zoom in on it.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: tool
  roles:
    ranks:
    - tool
    - drug_class
    - gene_symbol
    abundance: hits

- component: card
  title: Hits by drug class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of resistance gene hits, and the bars rank the drug classes that account for most of them. It answers which resistance classes dominate.
    How to read: a class leading the ranking is the main resistance signal. Names come from each tool's own vocabulary and are not merged, so a class can be split across spellings.
  column: hits
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: drug_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: hits, by drug class

- component: card
  title: Distinct resistance genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene symbols found, and the bars rank the screening tools by how many distinct genes each reports. It answers how rich the resistome is and which tool contributes most.
    How to read: a tool far ahead of the others may use a broader database or looser cut-offs. Gene symbols are not harmonised between tools, so the same gene can be counted twice under different names.
  column: gene_symbol
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: tool
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: distinct genes, by tool
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Sequence identity of hits
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent identity between a hit and its reference gene, and the box shows the spread. It answers how close the detected genes are to known resistance genes.
    How to read: identities near 100 percent mean confident, well characterised matches. A tail of low identities holds divergent homologues that deserve a look before being counted as resistance.
    Note: tools define identity at the nucleotide or amino acid level, so values are not strictly comparable across tools.
  column: identity_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Coverage of hits
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percent of the reference gene covered by a hit, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how complete the detected genes are.
    How to read: a pile at 100 percent means complete genes. A tail of partial hits holds fragments, which may be truncated genes or hits on a contig edge.
    Note: hAMRonization does not set a coverage threshold and each screening tool applies its own, so no pass mark is drawn here.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  column: coverage_pct
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average, with its median and minimum

- component: table
  title: Resistance gene hits
  description: |-
    Each row is a hit reported by one screening tool, with the sample, gene, drug class, database, coverage, identity and position on its contig. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: filter by tool to compare what each one found, or by gene to see every sample that carries it.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_symbol

- component: advanced_viz
  id: arg_upset
  title: Contig overlap between tools
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the contigs found by one exact combination of screening tools, and the dots below show which tools are in it. It answers which tools agree on where resistance genes are, and which find hits no other tool does.
    How to read: tall bars with many dots are contigs confirmed by several tools. Tall bars with one dot are tool specific, which can be a database difference or a false positive. Colour shows how many tools agree.
    Note: agreement is scored on the contig because every tool has its own gene vocabulary while the contig id is shared.
    Source: https://github.com/pha4ge/hAMRonization/
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree
    show_values: true

- component: table
  title: Contig by tool membership
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig with a 0 or 1 flag per screening tool. It answers which tools found resistance genes on a given contig.
    How to read: filter to one sample or to contigs found by a single tool to inspect disagreements.
